subject: Sizing request: Luminex dedicated footprint & quantization impact
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@luminex.ai>

Cc: Ravi Shah <ravi@luminex.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing request: Luminex dedicated footprint (80k context use case)

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We're progressing toward a procurement decision and need a concrete sizing / capacity recommendation for a Dedicated pool tied to the LNMX-487 POC. A few constraints:

- Primary model: custom 14B variant (sparse attention / proprietary tokenizer).
- Typical live requests: 250 qps peak, 30 qps baseline.
- Avg prompt + response token length: 12k combined; we plan to support up to 80k context for long-document retrieval use-cases (KV cache enabled).
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 600ms for user-facing inference.
- Expected concurrency per user session: 1-2 steady; bursts during batch ingestion.

Can you send a short note with: 1) KV cache memory per concurrent connection at 80k, 2) memory/instance sizing assuming 2 model variants (fp16 baseline / q4_0 quantized), and 3) high-level recommended dedicated pod count for a production commit (monthly committed throughput). I've attached a small workload CSV and a sample of cached keys.

Elena

Attachments: Luminex_ML_workload.csv (workload sample), kv_cache_sample.jsonl (KV entries)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@luminex.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing request: Luminex dedicated footprint (80k context use case)

Elena —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the attachments — useful. High level answers up front, then quick back-of-envelope details. We should schedule a 30-min call to validate traffic distributions and to look at a few sample traces, but this will give your procurement and infra folks a ballpark for budgeting.

Quick summary (ballpark):
- KV cache (80k tokens) per concurrent session: ~3.4–4.8 GB (depends on hidden size & dtype). This assumes a 2048 hidden dim baseline and storing key+value (float16).
- Model memory footprint (no activation memory): FP16 model weights + optimizations: ~42–48 GB for the 14B variant. Activation and KV overhead pushes working set toward ~90–120 GB for large contexts on a single instance without quantization.
- With q4_0 quantization we expect ~35–40% reduction in weight memory; combined with activation caching and prefix-KV caching strategies, per-instance working set drops to ~55–75 GB.
- Pod recommendation (production reserved): for 250 qps peak with 600ms p95 and our batching, a conservative starting pool is 6–8 GPUs (A100 80GB class) if using fp16, or 4–6 GPUs if you commit to q4_0 quantization and accept the ~3–4% risk in end-generation quality for some prompts.

Notes & assumptions:
- Above KV numbers assume we materialize KV for full 80k sequence for warm sessions; we can trade memory for latency by offloading older KV pages to NVMe with marginal impact on p95 if designed carefully.
- We used a hidden dim of 2048 and 32-bit attention key/value accumulation reduced to float16 storage. Different architecture (larger hidden dim) scales linearly.
- If you need strict deterministic FP16/FP32 equivalence, quantization may not be an option; we'll size accordingly.

I've attached a short spreadsheet (summary rows) — will follow up with an illustrated slide that breaks down math and pod counts. Would you and Ravi be available for a quick call this afternoon?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Sizing request: Luminex dedicated footprint (80k context use case)

Folks —

Quick engineering note to supplement Mina's numbers. I crunched a few more conservative estimates using our quantization benchmarks and model-splitting options:

- Model specifics used: 14B, hidden=2048, 32 layers. Weight memory (FP16): ~44GB. Activation + working set for 80k: additional ~48–64GB depending on caching strategy.
- KV cache math: 80k tokens * (k/v pair size ~ 64 bytes per token after pack) -> ~5.1GB per live session; margin added for metadata and alignment gives ~5.5GB. Our earlier float16 estimate accounted for different packing; both are in the same order.
- Quantization impact: q8_0 yields ~20–25% weight reduction but limited tooling maturity; q4_0 is stable and yields ~38–42% reduction in model weight. Real-world latency improvement for generation is ~10–25% depending on kernel support on target GPU.
- Pod sizing: If Luminex is conservative on quality, go fp16 with 8x A100-80GB (auto-scale to 10 during daytime burst). If they accept q4_0, 5x A100-80GB with HV autoscale policies should suffice for steady-state commit.

Operational options to present in the deck:
1) FP16 dedicated pool + NVMe KV offload for long tail sessions (recommended if quality is highest priority).
2) Quantized pool (q4_0) + selective high-fidelity fallback routes (for sensitive prompts).
3) Hybrid: reserve 4 GPU high-fidelity + 4 quantized for bulk traffic and automatic reroute on perf regressions.

I'll draft the slide that shows per-GPU token/sec curves and cost delta vs committed monthly spend.

-Aditya

On the quote lines in scope_redline_v1.pdf I added a conservative buffer for pod headroom (20%).
